minor.issue: Returns raw dollar amount as float (25.0) but the pending amount comes from stored cents/100. Fine, just noting that a $0.99 amount would be blocked at checkout by cents<100 check, so the /100 division is safe.

`amount` is a float — accepts negative values only implicitly (cents = int(round(neg*100)) would be < 100 so 400 fires). Consider explicit min via Pydantic conint/Field(gt=0) for clarity, but functional today.
Unpaginated to_list(500) hardcoded; fine for MVP but will eventually truncate.
donor_name is sliced [:80] in Stripe metadata but stored full-length in payment_transactions.donor_name — angel wall uses stored value, so a very long name could leak past the intended cap.

recipient_name is exposed even while pending (not gated by `paid`) — likely intentional (giver can see who they addressed the gift to on the success page), but note it differs from recipient_phone / activation_code which are hidden until paid.

recipient_phone is stored as raw string with only .strip(); no format normalization (e.g. E.164) or basic digit-length validation. Since the giver texts the link, a garbled phone would just fail silently later.

Uses `db.gifts.update_one({status:'pending'}, ...)`; if a webhook and a status-poll race, only one updates gift status — but the guard in payment_transactions.update_one (payment_status!='paid') already prevents double-angel or double-gift. Safe.

critical_code_review_comments: _finalize_paid correctly distinguishes donation vs gift via txn.type and inserts angels only on donation. Logic is idempotent thanks to the payment_status!='paid' guard in the update_one filter. Good.

BLESSING_SCRIPTURES is chosen at random *at every /donations/status call after paid*, so consecutive polls after payment can show different blessings to the same donor. If product wants a stable blessing per donor, persist the chosen blessing on the payment_transactions or angels record.
recipient_email is now optional but empty string is stored as ''.lower() (fine) — consider storing None instead of '' for cleanliness so downstream 'if gift.recipient_email' checks work as expected.

GET /api/angels returns only name+created_at (amount excluded). If the product wants to display a total-raised badge on the wall, expose an aggregate (or a per-angel amount) — currently only `total` count is returned.
Donation route has no rate limiting; someone could spam POST /api/donations/checkout to create many Stripe sessions (no charge, but noise). Consider a per-IP throttle for MVP hardening.
server.py has grown to 815 lines. Splitting into routers (auth, counsel, diary, gifts, donations, testimonies) is still recommended (was called out in iter1).
activate_gift still grants a flat 30 days without extending from an existing subscription_expires_at (call-out from iter1, unchanged).
seed_data_creation: Created ~4 pending Stripe test sessions this run (2 donations from TEST_Grace/TEST_Anon at $25 and $5, 1 gift with phone TEST_John/5551234567, plus regression gift + testimony TEST_Storyteller). None are charged; they stay as unpaid cs_test_ sessions. All test data uses TEST_ prefix or fresh_user_<uuid>@wwjdtest.io emails and can be left in place.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Full suite: `REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=<preview> pytest tests/test_wwjd_backend.py -v` from /app/backend. It exercises real Stripe test key (creates cs_test_ sessions each run — never charges), real Claude Sonnet 4.6 (~15-30s per SSE turn), real Emergent object storage. To exercise the paid path for donations (which is required to see a real 'angel' inserted and a blessing returned), complete the checkout in a real browser with card 4242 4242 4242 4242 — this is intentionally NOT done headlessly. The _finalize_paid function has been code-reviewed and is correct: donations -> insert angels, gifts -> mark gift status paid, both branches idempotent via update_one guard.
